issues.detail: The Hebrew 'דֹּם' (be silent/be still) is omitted; the Chinese only renders 'הֵאָנֵק' (groan/sigh) as '不要哀號' but does not convey the command to be silent.

The Hebrew 'וְלֹא תַעְטֶה עַל שָׂפָם' means 'and you shall not cover your upper lip' (a mourning custom), but the Chinese renders it as '不可剃掉鬍子' (do not shave off the beard), which is a different action not present in the Hebrew.
